mechanism: Aflibercept biosimilar candidate for intravitreal use. Aflibercept is a VEGF inhibitor that acts as a soluble decoy receptor binding VEGF-A and placental growth factor, inhibiting activation of VEGF receptors involved in neovascularization and vascular permeability.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06470373 as a not-yet-recruiting, randomized, double-masked Phase 3 equivalence study comparing RBS-001 with Eylea in 434 subjects with neovascular age-related macular degeneration, with estimated start July 2025 and estimated primary/study completion September 2026. The EU CTIS record for the related EU trial lists the trial as ended with global end of trial on 2025-04-18, creating a timing/status discrepancy that should be monitored.
expected_launch_window: 2028-2029, contingent on actual Phase 3 execution and BLA timing
clinical_summary: RBS-001 is being developed as an Eylea aflibercept biosimilar, so the clinical thesis is equivalence rather than superior efficacy, durability, safety, or route. The Phase 3 study is designed to compare efficacy, safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity versus Eylea, with the primary endpoint of BCVA change from baseline by ETDRS letters at 8 weeks after treatment. No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted. Current differentiation is mainly potential access/cost competition in an already crowded aflibercept biosimilar market.
safety_summary: No RBS-001 human results are posted in ClinicalTrials.gov. Safety expectations are inferred from aflibercept and the biosimilar-equivalence design: the trial compares safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity versus Eylea. Eylea labeling warns of endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis, intraocular pressure increases, and thromboembolic events after intravitreal VEGF inhibition; these are relevant class and procedure risks to monitor for RBS-001.
management_tools: Medical benefit prior authorization aligned to wet AMD diagnosis, anti-VEGF appropriateness, and retinal specialist administration
Lowest-net-cost preferred aflibercept product or biosimilar step policy after approval, label, interchangeability status, and contracting review
Continuation criteria based on maintenance or improvement in BCVA, visual field, retinal fluid, or reduced vision-loss risk
Dose and frequency edits tied to labeled 2 mg intravitreal regimen and eye-level billing
Contracting watch across Eylea, Eylea HD, approved aflibercept biosimilars, Vabysmo, ranibizumab biosimilars, and bevacizumab pathways
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT06470373.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists the trial as not yet recruiting with estimated completion September 2026, while CTIS lists the EU trial as ended with global end of trial on 2025-04-18.
No FDA approval, proposed U.S. proprietary name, interchangeability designation, launch date, or U.S. price was found for RBS-001.
The company July 2024 press release targeted Phase 3 completion in December 2025 and revenue in 2026-2027 after BLA, but current ClinicalTrials.gov dates are later.
Final payer impact depends on net contracting versus already approved aflibercept biosimilars and whether RBS-001 receives an interchangeability designation.

sources.title: A Phase 3 Clinical Trial to Compare RBS-001 to Eylea in Subjects With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: Sponsor is Rophibio, Inc.; organization class is industry.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; last update posted was 2025-04-06 and status was verified in April 2025.
Study is a randomized, double-masked, parallel Phase 3 trial in 434 subjects with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
Estimated study start is July 2025; estimated primary completion and study completion are September 2026.
The study compares RBS-001 Solution for intravitreal injection with Eylea Solution for intravitreal injection.
Both arms administer 2 mg/eye (50 uL/eye) per dose by intravitreal injection to the study eye.
Primary endpoint is change in BCVA measured by ETDRS letter score from baseline to 8 weeks after investigational product treatment.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: A Clinical Trial to compare Efficacy, Safety, Tolerability of RBS-001 to Eylea in Subjects with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: EU CTIS trial number is 2023-509206-29-00 with protocol code PD-CP-Y1.
Sponsor is Rophibio Inc.; trial phase is therapeutic confirmatory Phase III.
CTIS lists medical condition as neovascular age-related macular degeneration and planned participants as 434.
Main objective is to demonstrate equivalence of RBS-001 and Eylea for BCVA change from baseline by ETDRS letter score at 8 weeks after treatment.

RBS-001 product details list pharmaceutical form as solution for intravitreal injection, route as intravitreal use, sponsor product code RBS-001, active substance aflibercept, and product authorization status not authorised.
Maximum treatment duration is 48 weeks, maximum daily dose is 2 mg, and maximum total dose is 16 mg.
CTIS lists overall status ended, end of trial 2025-04-17, and global end of trial 2025-04-18.
Locations include Bulgaria, Croatia, Poland, Slovakia, and countries outside the EEA including Korea, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, and the United States.

sources.title: Rophibio receives Korea MFDS Phase 3 plan approval for Eylea biosimilar RBS-001 after U.S. FDA and Europe EMA approvals
supports: Company press release identifies RBS-001 as an Eylea biosimilar.
Rophibio stated that U.S. FDA, Europe EMA, and Korea MFDS Phase 3 plans were approved.
The Phase 3 plan was to compare efficacy, safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity between RBS-001 and Eylea in neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration.
The company targeted Phase 3 completion in December 2025 and commercial revenue in 2026-2027 after a U.S. BLA, but current ClinicalTrials.gov dates are later.

sources.title: Amicogen says affiliate Rophibio received domestic Phase 3 plan approval for eye-disease biosimilar
supports: Yonhap reported that Amicogen affiliate Rophibio received Korea MFDS approval for the Phase 3 trial plan for RBS-001.
The report states RBS-001 is a biosimilar to Eylea, developed by Regeneron for wet AMD and diabetic macular edema.
The report states Rophibio planned to compare RBS-001 and the originator drug for efficacy, safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
The report states Rophibio had already received RBS-001 Phase 3 plan approvals from FDA and EMA.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA (aflibercept) injection, solution
supports: Eylea is a VEGF inhibitor indicated for neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration.
Recommended wet AMD dosing is 2 mg intravitreal injection every 4 weeks for the first 3 months, followed by 2 mg every 8 weeks.
Aflibercept acts as a soluble decoy receptor that binds VEGF-A and PlGF, inhibiting VEGF receptor activation.
Label warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachments, retinal vasculitis, intraocular pressure increases, and thromboembolic events.
Most common adverse reactions include conjunctival hemorrhage, eye pain, cataract, vitreous detachment, vitreous floaters, and increased intraocular pressure.

sources.title: Biosimilar Product Information
supports: FDA-approved aflibercept biosimilars listed for Eylea include Yesafili, Opuviz, Ahzantive, Enzeevu, Pavblu, and Eydenzelt.
RBS-001 is not listed among FDA-approved biosimilar products on the reviewed FDA biosimilar product information page.
FDA states biosimilar approvals can improve medication options and potentially lower costs.

sources.title: FDA approves first interchangeable biosimilars to Eylea to treat macular degeneration and other eye conditions
supports: FDA approved Yesafili and Opuviz as interchangeable biosimilars to Eylea.
FDA states aflibercept products inhibit VEGF to prevent abnormal blood-vessel growth within the eye.
FDA states approved aflibercept biosimilars are used to treat neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration and are administered intravitreally as 2 mg (0.05 mL of 40 mg/mL) injectable solution.

FDA states a biosimilar is highly similar to and has no clinically meaningful differences from the reference product, and patients can expect the same safety and effectiveness as the reference product.
FDA states biosimilar and interchangeable biosimilar products may cost less than the reference product.

sources.title: FDA and FTC Collaborate to Advance Competition in the Biologic Marketplace
supports: FDA states biosimilars can provide greater access and potentially reduce costs through market competition.
FDA cites report data showing average biosimilar sales price is less than half the reference product price at launch.
FDA notes market competition is leading to reduced costs for both biosimilar and reference products.

sources.title: CMS April 2026 Medicare Part B Payment Limit Files
supports: April 2026 CMS ASP file lists J0178 aflibercept injection at $731.885 per 1 mg.
A 2 mg aflibercept dose therefore maps to approximately $1,463.77 before add-ons, administration, bilateral use, or rebates.
Eight 2 mg doses, matching the CTIS 16 mg maximum total dose, maps to approximately $11,710 based on April 2026 ASP.

sources.title: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitors for Ocular Indications
supports: Aetna requires precertification for multiple ocular VEGF inhibitors including Eylea, Eylea HD, and approved aflibercept biosimilars in applicable plan designs.
Aetna considers intravitreal aflibercept products medically necessary for neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration when criteria are met.
Aetna allows brand selection or trial of lower-cost preferred drugs when lower-cost alternatives are at least as likely to produce equivalent therapeutic results.

Continuation of aflibercept therapy requires positive clinical response such as improvement or maintenance in BCVA or visual field, or reduced rate of vision decline or risk of more severe vision loss.
Aetna summarizes aflibercept mechanism as binding VEGF-A isoforms and PlGF and preventing binding to VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2.

expected_launch_window.value: 2028-2029, contingent on actual Phase 3 execution and BLA timing
expected_launch_window.method: Derived from ClinicalTrials.gov estimated Phase 3 primary completion in September 2026 plus time for data readout, BLA preparation/review, and launch; tempered by CTIS ended status and not-yet-recruiting CT.gov status.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A late-2027 launch would require clean Phase 3 completion and rapid filing, while the registry discrepancy supports a more conservative 2028-2029 planning window.

annual_cost_range.method: High estimate approximates reference aflibercept first-year medical-benefit drug cost using CMS ASP $731.885 per mg x 2 mg x 8 doses = about $11,710, rounded upward to $16,000 to allow launch WAC/add-on uncertainty. Low estimate applies FDA-cited biosimilar launch pricing evidence of less than half the reference product price to the same eight-dose annual exposure, rounded to $6,000.
annual_cost_range.explanation: RBS-001 has no disclosed U.S. price. The range is a drug-acquisition planning proxy for one treated eye and excludes administration, bilateral treatment, imaging, office visits, rebates, and site-of-care effects.

clinical_differentiation.method: Assigned low because RBS-001 is an aflibercept biosimilar candidate being tested for equivalence to Eylea, not for superior efficacy, durability, safety, route, or dosing.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: The clinical value proposition is comparable efficacy/safety with potential access and net-cost benefits; no direct RBS-001 results are posted.

budget_impact.method: Balanced chronic high-spend anti-VEGF utilization against likely biosimilar price competition and potential displacement of higher-cost aflibercept products.
budget_impact.explanation: RBS-001 could matter for contracting and preferred-product strategy, but it is unlikely to increase clinical utilization materially if it is only biosimilar to Eylea.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed from near-term Phase 3/BLA potential, crowded aflibercept biosimilar contracting dynamics, and medical-benefit policy changes rather than novel clinical operations.
disruption_risk.explanation: Operational disruption would mainly involve formulary preference, PA edits, billing/coding, and retinal-specialist communication; clinical pathway disruption is limited by biosimilar equivalence.

recommended_action.method: Recommended preparation, not active implementation, because the asset is Phase 3 and potentially within a few years of launch but lacks posted results, approval, price, and final interchangeability status.
recommended_action.explanation: Plans should maintain a contracting and policy-ready stance for another aflibercept biosimilar while monitoring the CT.gov/CTIS status discrepancy and any BLA signal.

quality_flags: Registry discrepancy: ClinicalTrials.gov lists NCT06470373 as not yet recruiting with estimated completion September 2026, while CTIS lists the EU trial as ended with global end of trial on 2025-04-18.
RBS-001 is a biosimilar-equivalence asset; clinical differentiation should not be scored as meaningful absent evidence of superior efficacy, durability, safety, route, or dosing.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT06470373.
No FDA approval or U.S. price was found for RBS-001; annual cost is analog-derived from aflibercept ASP and biosimilar pricing evidence.
The aflibercept biosimilar market is already crowded with multiple FDA-approved Eylea biosimilars, so final impact depends on launch timing, interchangeability, and net contracting.
